title: Tasks and async/await
summary: Asynchronous code in C# - why waiting should not block a thread, Task and Task<T>, async methods and await, running work in sequence or at the same time with Task.WhenAll and WhenAny, exceptions in async code, async void and why to avoid it, ValueTask, async streams with IAsyncEnumerable, and never blocking with .Result.

cards.q: What does await do to the thread while the awaited task is not finished?
cards.a:
It frees the thread; the method resumes when the task is done

`await` returns control to the caller instead of blocking, so the thread can do other work. The rest of the method runs after the task completes.

cards.q: Why should you not call .Result on a task?
cards.a:
It blocks the thread, and on a UI thread it can deadlock

`.Result` waits by blocking, which wastes the thread. On a UI thread that can deadlock, because the task may need that very thread to finish; `await` instead.

cards.q: Two independent operations take 1 second each. How long does `await Task.WhenAll(A(), B())` take?
cards.a:
About 1 second

Both tasks are started before waiting, so they run at the same time.
